target: Execution plan item 1.3 and amendment log 2026-08-20: 'adjudication performed by Claude per Rehan's delegation' — the 80-case ground-truth adjudication that anchors the entire jury system, pathladder audit, and Ch4 label source was performed by the same LLM that designed the pipeline, wrote the extraction rules, and is co-authoring the thesis.
flaw: This is a textbook self-validation loop: the system whose output (pathladder) is being audited also adjudicates the audit truth. The 'independence caveat recorded for write-up' does not fix the epistemic problem — every downstream metric (jury Fleiss κ = 0.900, pathladder accuracy, Ch4 cross-evaluation) is calibrated against a machine-generated gold standard that shares systematic biases with the system under test. Rehan's spot-check of 10 cases is still pending and cannot retroactively validate 80 adjudications.
fix: An independent human pathologist (not Rehan, not Claude) must adjudicate at least the 80 cases plus a random sample of 50 jury-disagreement reports before any downstream result is cited as validated. Until then, all metrics anchored on these labels must be labelled 'provisional, machine-adjudicated'.

target: ERIN Ch3 pre-registration primary endpoint: 'current-biopsy grade classification — NDBE vs {LGD, HGD, CANCER}' with histology-only AUC 0.9255 (erin_encoder_sweep.json). The pre-registration itself names the risk: 'probable label leakage: grade is itself report-derived'.
flaw: The labels were extracted from pathology reports written by pathologists who looked at the same H&E slides the model is trained on. The model is not discovering independent biological signal; it is learning to reverse-engineer what a pathologist wrote about the image it is seeing. An AUC of 0.93 on this task is expected under circularity and cannot be interpreted as evidence that histology contains prognostic information beyond what the report already captures. The 'mitigation' (using only PRIOR-timepoint clinical variables in arm 2) addresses the clinical arm but not the label itself.
fix: The primary endpoint must be redefined as progression (a future event not derivable from the current slide), which the pre-registration already lists as secondary. Alternatively, obtain expert re-grades on a subset blinded to the original report and report model performance against those independent labels. The current grade-classification AUC should be reported only as a feasibility check with an explicit circularity caveat.

target: SWG arm headline claim: 'late-mean fusion is the best family' selected from seven on the same data, then the fusion-vs-histology contrast reported as the thesis's 'strongest fusion contrast'. The encoder-conditional caveat (latemean_vs_gigapath_paired.json: ΔAUPRC CI [−0.064, 0.104], ΔAUC CI [−0.020, 0.103], both crossing zero) is disclosed but the multiplicity plan states 'No optimism correction is attempted at n=150'.
flaw: Two compounding biases inflate this result: (1) winner's curse from selecting the best family on the evaluation data, and (2) the contrast vanishes against the strongest unimodal encoder. The thesis's central positive fusion claim rests on a comparison against a deliberately weak baseline (UNI2 histology-only) while the best available unimodal comparator (GigaPath) nullifies it. Reporting this as 'the strongest fusion contrast in the release' is misleading when the strength is an artefact of baseline choice.
fix: Report the fusion claim exclusively against the best unimodal encoder (GigaPath), which is the honest comparator. If only Brier survives, the claim must be 'fusion improves calibration but not discrimination'. Additionally, apply a simple optimism correction: re-select the best family on inner folds only and report the outer-fold contrast, or use the pre-registered primary (fusion-vs-CNV) as the headline and demote fusion-vs-histology to exploratory.

target: OCCAMS v3 (occams_v3.json, n=87): execution plan item 1.1 records 'deviation: shuffled controls omitted'. The v2 results (occams_fusion_v2.json) show gen_only shuffled_auc = 0.581, already above 0.5, and hist_only shuffled_auc = 0.457, below 0.5.
flaw: The pre-registered decision tree (occams_v2_decision_tree.md, Outcome D) explicitly states that a shuffled control away from 0.5 'invalidates the pipeline, not the hypothesis'. The v2 shuffled controls were already anomalous (genomics shuffle at 0.58 suggests label leakage or a pipeline bug), and v3 omitted them entirely. Without valid controls, the C-indices reported (hist 0.627, fusion 0.589) cannot be distinguished from artefacts. The n=87 result is uninterpretable.
fix: Run shuffled-label controls for all v3 arms immediately. If any deviate from 0.5 by more than the pre-registered tolerance, debug the pipeline before citing any OCCAMS v3 number. The omission must be reported as a protocol violation in the thesis, not merely 'noted for write-up'.

target: ERIN encoder sweep (erin_encoder_sweep.json): UNI2 late-fusion delta = +0.0059, 95% CI [−0.005, 0.0175] — includes zero. The pre-registration states 'Fusion benefit: paired fusion-minus-histology delta CI excluding zero' as the criterion for claiming replication.
flaw: The pre-registered primary configuration (UNI2 + ABMIL) fails to demonstrate fusion benefit on the primary endpoint by the pre-registered criterion. The CI includes zero. Meanwhile, Virchow2 and GigaPath show significant positive deltas — the opposite of the expected pattern where the primary encoder should be at least as good. This means Ch3 cannot claim 'fusion benefit on primary → Ch3's claim replicates externally at 16× scale'. The result is, by the pre-registration's own logic, 'Signal without fusion benefit', which the pre-registration says should be reported as 'an informative negative'.
fix: Report Ch3's primary result as the pre-registration dictates: signal present (histology AUC 0.93) but fusion benefit not demonstrated on the primary encoder. Investigate why UNI2 underperforms Virchow2/GigaPath for fusion (possible feature-scale mismatch in the late-fusion combiner). The chapter's claim must be downgraded accordingly.

target: Jury composition (jury_corpus_analysis.json): 8 models, all ≤32B parameters (qwen3 14b/32b, gemma3 12b/27b, phi4 14b, deepseek-r1 14b, mistral-small3.2, llama3.1 8b). Fleiss κ = 0.900 cited as evidence of label reliability.
flaw: High inter-model agreement among architecturally similar, similarly-sized, contemporaneously-trained models does not validate against ground truth — it validates against shared training-data biases. The jury lacks any model >32B (llama3.3:70b is still 'pending'), any model from a fundamentally different training paradigm, or any human pathologist. The 0.900 κ is presented as if it measures reliability against truth, but it measures homogeneity of bias. The 80-case adjudicated anchor was itself produced by Claude (see criticism #1), so the entire validation chain is circular.
fix: Include at least one ≥70B model and one domain-tuned model (medgemma, as already planned in 2.18) before finalising labels. More critically, obtain pathologist grades on a stratified sample of ≥250 reports (item R.4, already flagged as REQUIRED in the review) and report jury-vs-pathologist agreement separately from jury-vs-jury agreement. The Fleiss κ should be reported as a homogeneity metric, not a validity metric.

target: Necessity probes (necessity_probes.json, n=446): TP53 AUC 0.678, WGD AUC 0.703 from H&E. Amendment log: 'the pooled gain arrives with a population change'. Evaluation protocol: 'the OAC-only replication at comparable n remains unresolved (its shuffled control failed)'. TCGA probe (tcga_probe.json): TP53 AUC 0.355 (below chance), null_mean 0.474.
flaw: The positive visibility result is confounded by mixing OAC with STAD/GEJ (different histology, different molecular profiles), and the clean OAC-only replication at comparable n has a broken shuffled control. The TCGA-OAC-only probe produces anti-predictive results (AUC 0.355 < 0.5), which is a red flag for systematic label or feature misalignment. The thesis currently has no valid test of genotype visibility in a single population at adequate n.
fix: Debug the TCGA probe pipeline until the shuffled control produces AUC ≈ 0.5 (item 1.17, already identified). Only then can the OAC-only visibility question be answered. Until then, the pooled n=446 result must be labelled 'population-confounded, exploratory' and the Ch2 Part A narrative must not cite it as evidence that genomics is visible from H&E in OAC specifically.

target: OCCAMS n=87 vs planned n=141 (execution plan item 1.1: 'n=87 vs planned 141 needs explanation under 1.12'). The v2 metadata shows 'early_censored_excluded': 257 from an original pool, and the v3 metadata shows n=87 with 58 events.
flaw: A 38% attrition from the pre-registered sample size is noted but never explained. The decision tree was calibrated for n≈141; at n=87 the bootstrap CIs widen substantially (hist C CI: [0.539, 0.711] — barely above the 0.55 signal threshold). If the 54 excluded patients differ systematically from the 87 retained (e.g., earlier-stage patients censored before the 730-day window), the results are biased. The plan says this 'needs explanation' but no explanation exists in any provided document.
fix: Produce a CONSORT-style attrition flow showing exactly how 141 became 87, with reasons for each exclusion. Compare baseline characteristics (stage, age, treatment) of included vs excluded patients. If exclusions are informative (e.g., early deaths from aggressive disease), the analysis must be re-run with a censoring-aware method that accommodates them, or the limitation must be stated as potentially biasing.

target: ERIN clinical-only arm (erin_encoder_sweep.json): clin_only AUC 0.7562, using 'report-derived structured variables (age, surveillance interval, prior-grade history, cancer-pathway flag)'. The labels are also report-derived grades.
flaw: The clinical arm's features and the target labels share a common source (pathology reports). 'Prior-grade history' is particularly problematic: if a patient's prior report said 'HGD' and the current label is 'HGD', the clinical arm has near-direct access to the answer through temporal autocorrelation. The pre-registration's mitigation ('only PRIOR-timepoint clinical variables') does not address this because prior grades are the strongest predictor of current grade by construction — this is not leakage from the future, it is leakage from the same reporting process.
fix: Report the clinical arm's performance stratified by whether the prior grade matches the current label. If the AUC drops substantially in the mismatch stratum, the arm is capturing reporting inertia, not independent clinical signal. Alternatively, restrict the clinical arm to non-grade variables (age, surveillance interval only) and report the grade-history version separately as a sensitivity analysis.

target: Multiplicity plan (multiplicity_plan.md): 'One confirmatory contrast per chapter, declared here; everything else is exploratory.' But the SWG arm alone reports fusion-vs-CNV (AUPRC, AUC, Brier), fusion-vs-histology-UNI2 (AUPRC, AUC, Brier), and fusion-vs-histology-GigaPath (AUPRC, AUC, Brier) — 9 paired contrasts on one cohort, of which only 1 is 'confirmatory'.
flaw: The confirmatory/exploratory distinction is doing excessive work. The SWG chapter's actual narrative claim ('fusion beats histology') is supported by the fusion-vs-histology contrast, which is labelled confirmatory, but the selection of which contrast to call confirmatory was made after seeing that fusion-vs-CNV had a wider CI. The Holm correction over 4 contrasts (one per chapter) is too lenient when each chapter reports multiple metrics on its confirmatory contrast, and the 'exploratory' label on the GigaPath comparison is strategically convenient since it is the one that nullifies the claim.
fix: Pre-specify which metric (AUC, AUPRC, or Brier) is the single primary for each confirmatory contrast, and apply Holm over the 4 primary metrics only. The GigaPath comparison must be labelled 'pre-specified sensitivity analysis' rather than 'exploratory', since it was designed before results existed (per the encoder-sweep pre-registration) and its outcome directly constrains the chapter's claim.

target: Progression cohort definition change: erin_consensus_final.json reports 'progression_cohort_n: 1218, progressors: 197' while erin_jury_labels_summary.json reports 'progression_v3: patients: 1266, progressors: 181'. The execution plan amendment says the old grader 'inflated progression events ~30% via false CANCER calls'.
flaw: The relabelling changed both the denominator (+48 patients) and the numerator (−16 progressors, an 8% reduction). The direction is concerning: removing false CANCER calls should reduce progressors, but adding 48 patients while losing 16 progressors means the new cohort has a lower event rate (14.3% vs 16.2%), which reduces power for the progression endpoint. More importantly, the definition of 'progressor' has silently changed between versions without a pre-registered amendment specifying the new inclusion criteria, making it unclear whether the two cohorts are comparable.
fix: Document the exact inclusion/exclusion criteria for progression cohort v3 vs the original, showing which patients entered and which progressors were lost and why. Pre-register the v3 criteria before running Ch3's progression model. Report both versions' event rates and confirm that the power calculation for the secondary endpoint still holds at 181 events.

target: Execution plan item 2.21: 'thesis red-team review — local model jury (4 models) + one fresh-context Claude agent critique the plan, drafts, pre-registrations and results digest'. The amendment log states the review produced 'five independent reviewers across four model families converged that no cohort shows fusion beating the best unimodal arm'.
flaw: The quality-assurance mechanism is itself an LLM jury, creating a closed epistemic loop: Claude designs the work, Claude executes it, Claude adjudicates the ground truth, and Claude (plus similar models) reviews the output. The 'convergence' of five LLM reviewers is not independent validation — it is the same phenomenon as the model jury's high Fleiss κ (shared biases produce agreement). No human with domain expertise has reviewed the results digest, the pre-registrations, or the chapter drafts at any point documented in these materials.
fix: Before thesis submission, at least one domain expert (a computational pathologist or biostatistician not involved in the project) must review the results digest and pre-registrations and produce a written critique. The LLM red-team review should be reported in the thesis as a pilot exercise with explicit caveats about its limitations, not as evidence of robustness.
